title: Unit econ dashboard: RBAC for restricted slices + audit logging for access
author: Marcus Lin
release_notes:
- Restricted unit economics views (discount/credit impact + account-level slices) now require explicit roles
- All restricted queries are audit-logged with actor + policy decision metadata
- Console shows a clear “restricted view” banner and links to access request process
description: Title: Unit econ dashboard: RBAC for restricted slices + audit logging for access Context: As we roll the internal unit economics dashboard out to a wider set of users, we need to restrict slices that expose pricing/discount/credit impacts and any account-level drilldowns. Finance also requested an audit trail for compliance and for investigating “who saw what” questions. This PR implements role-based access control for restricted unit-econ query dimensions/metrics and adds immutable audit logs for all access to restricted views. Linked: ENG-2921, PM-484; support/internal request: INT-2210. What’s restricted: (1) Metrics: discounted_blended_cost_usd, credits_usd, effective_rate_usd_per_1m_out (anything that incorporates discounts/credits); (2) Dimensions: account_id/account_name, contract_id, negotiated_tier, discount_program; (3) Exports: CSV exports that include any restricted fields. Non-restricted (default) views remain accessible to the existing internal audience: blended_cost_usd_per_1m_out, compute_cost_usd, overhead_alloc_usd, cache_savings_est_usd aggregated by {date, model, region, customer_tier}. Authorization model: We use Redwood’s internal authz middleware with a simple role mapping from the identity token (groups claim). New roles: unit_econ_restricted_viewer (can query restricted slices but cannot export), unit_econ_restricted_exporter (can query + export restricted slices), unit_econ_admin (can manage feature flags / override for incident response; still audited). Policy lives in code under console-backend so the decision is consistently enforced at the API boundary; we also added a guard in the semantic layer query builder to avoid accidental inclusion of restricted columns in “safe” endpoints. Audit logging: Any request that triggers restricted policy evaluation emits an audit event to audit_log_events with: actor_user_id, actor_email, actor_groups, request_id, ip, user_agent, endpoint, policy_name, policy_result (allow/deny), restricted_fields (canonical names), query_fingerprint (sha256 of normalized query JSON), time_range, row_count (if allowed), export (true/false). Important: we do NOT log raw filters that may contain customer identifiers beyond the canonical dimension names; account_id values are not written to the audit log. Query_fingerprint lets us correlate repeated access without storing PII-heavy parameters. UX: Console UI now shows a “Restricted data” banner when restricted fields are in play and surfaces a helpful error when denied (403 with an access-request link). Export button is disabled unless user has unit_econ_restricted_exporter. Tests: Added unit tests for policy evaluation (matrix across roles), integration tests for /internal/unit-econ/query and /internal/unit-econ/export ensuring restricted columns are rejected for non-authorized callers, and audit-log emission tests (allow + deny). Rollout: Behind feature flag unit_econ_rbac_enforcement (default ON in staging, OFF in prod until Finance sign-off). Audit logging is ON regardless of the enforcement flag for any restricted attempt (deny events are important too). Follow-ups (out of scope): (a) Backfill audit logs to the security lake (separate pipeline); (b) Fine-grained per-field entitlements by org/team; (c) UI for requesting access. Commits: 1) console-backend: add unit econ policy + enforcement middleware 2) analytics: restrict semantic layer column allowlist; safe query builder 3) console-ui: restricted banner + export gating + denied state copy 4) audit: add audit_log_events emitter + tests 5) docs: internal runbook updates for access requests + auditing FAQ Changed areas/files (high level): - services/console-backend/src/authz/policies/unit_econ_restricted.ts (new) - services/console-backend/src/routes/unit_econ.ts (enforce policy; emit audit) - services/console-backend/src/audit/audit_logger.ts (new; shared helper) - services/analytics/semantic-layer/unit_econ_views.sql (restricted column tagging; allowlist) - services/console-ui/pages/unit-economics/* (restricted banner + export gating) - db/migrations/20250210_add_audit_log_events.sql (new table for audit events) - docs/runbooks/unit-econ-access-and-auditing.md (new) Review notes: - Please sanity check the restricted field list with Finance (Laura / Rishi) and the access request language with Naomi. - SRE: audit log table is append-only; retention is 400 days per compliance default; size impact is small (restricted queries should be low volume). CI: build-and-test (pass), lint (pass), console-ui unit (pass), console-backend integration (pass), sql-validate (pass).
review_conversation: Naomi Feldman: Can we confirm that “customer_tier” is not considered restricted? Finance asked to keep tier visible broadly but hide discount impacts. Also please ensure the 403 message doesn’t leak restricted field names in the UI screenshot shares. Marcus Lin (author): Confirmed: customer_tier is non-restricted. Only negotiated_tier and discount_program are restricted. Updated UI to show a generic message; detailed restricted_fields remain in server logs/audit only. Chloe Martin: Two asks: (1) enforce restriction in export endpoint too (not just query), (2) please ensure the audit logger doesn’t include raw filter JSON for account_id. Marcus Lin (author): Added explicit policy check in /export and normalized query hashing; removed raw filter logging. Added tests that assert account_id not present in audit payload. Priya Natarajan: Policy override worries me—what stops unit_econ_admin from being used casually? Can we require an incident ID when using override? Marcus Lin (author): Good call. Added optional header X-Redwood-Incident-Id; when role=unit_econ_admin and restricted access is allowed, audit entry includes incident_id (required in prod via config). Aisha Bello: Please add an alert if audit logging fails (we should not silently drop events). Marcus Lin (author): Added metric audit_logger_write_fail_total and wired to existing alert policy (non-paging for now; paging if >5/min). Laura Bennett: Looks aligned. Please make sure export is only for Finance and that the audit log includes actor_email + time range. Marcus Lin (author): Export role separated; time range is logged in a normalized form (start/end day). Approved. Approvals: Naomi Feldman (approved), Chloe Martin (approved), Priya Natarajan (approved), Aisha Bello (approved), Laura Bennett (approved).
